props.gloss_en: R' Yosei bar Chanina: priestly and Levitical families cancel their service and come to hear the reading of the Megilla
R' Yosei bar Chanina: the words 'every family' (Esther 9:28) come to include the priestly and Levitical families
Rav: priests at their service, Levites on their platform and Israelites at their maamad -- all cancel their service and come to hear the Megilla
the baraita: priests, Levites and Israelites at their posts all cancel their service to hear the Megilla
the house of Rabbi relied on this: one cancels Torah study and comes to hear the Megilla
the verse (Josh 5:13-14): Joshua saw a man standing before him ... and bowed down
RYbL: one may not greet his fellow at night -- we are concerned it may be a demon
the stam: there it was different, for he said to him 'I am captain of the host of the Lord'
the angel: last evening you neglected the afternoon tamid, and now you have neglected Torah study
Joshua asked for which of these he had come; the angel: 'I have come now' -- for the present one, the neglect of Torah study
at once: 'and Joshua lodged that night in the midst of the valley' (Josh 8:9, 8:13)
R' Yochanan: this teaches that he lodged in the depth of halakha
Rav Shmuel bar Unya: Torah study is greater than offering the daily offerings
Rav Shmuel bar Unya's verse: 'I have come now' (Josh 5:14)
the mishna: on the intermediate days women lament in unison but do not clap
R' Yishmael: those close to the bier may clap
the mishna: on New Moons, Chanukka and Purim they lament and clap; on both, they do not wail responsively
Rabba bar Huna: there is no Moed in the presence of [a deceased] Torah scholar -- all the more so Chanukka and Purim
Rava: service vs the Megilla reading -- the Megilla takes precedence
Rava: Torah study vs the Megilla reading -- the Megilla takes precedence
Rava: Torah study vs a met mitzva -- the met mitzva takes precedence
the baraita: one cancels Torah study to bring out the dead and to bring in a bride
Rava: service vs a met mitzva -- the met mitzva takes precedence, from 'or for his sister'
the baraita: one going to slaughter his paschal lamb or circumcise his son who heard a relative died -- might he become impure? you said: he shall not
the baraita: 'or for his sister' (Bamidbar 6:7) -- for his sister he does not become impure, but he does for a met mitzva
(the iba'ya's first side) the Megilla takes precedence, for publicising the miracle
Rava, resolving his own iba'ya: the met mitzva takes precedence over the Megilla
as the Master said: great is human dignity, for it overrides a prohibition of the Torah
RYbL: a walled city, and whatever is adjacent to it or seen with it, is judged as a walled city
the tanna: adjacent -- even though it is not seen
the tanna: seen -- even though it is not adjacent
the stam: seen-though-not-adjacent is found where it sits on a hilltop
R' Yirmeya: adjacent-though-not-seen is one that sits in a valley
RYbL: a walled city first settled and only later walled is judged as a village
the stam: the reason is the verse 'and if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city' (Vayikra 25:29)
the criterion read from the verse: 'a dwelling-place of a walled city' is one walled first and settled afterwards
the bridge: and not one settled first and walled afterwards -- the case lacks the criterion
RYbL: a walled city without ten batlanim is judged as a village
the mishna (5a): a large city is any with ten batlanim; fewer -- it is a village
taught by the dictum's mention of a krakh: even if idlers happen to come there from elsewhere, it is a village
RYbL: a walled city destroyed and later resettled is judged as a walled city
(proposed) 'destroyed' means its walls were destroyed -- so resettled yes, not resettled no
R' Eliezer bar Yosei: 'which has [lo] a wall' (Vayikra 25:30) -- even though it has none now, if it had one before
the stam: rather, 'destroyed' means destroyed of its ten batlanim
RYbL: Lod, Ono and Gei HaCharashim were walled since the days of Joshua son of Nun
the stam: Elpaal built them, as written (Divrei HaYamim I 8:12)
R' Elazar: they were destroyed in the days of the concubine at Givea and Elpaal rebuilt them; they fell again and Asa restored them
the stam: 'let us build these cities' (Divrei HaYamim II 14:6) implies they were cities from the outset
RYbL: women are obligated in the reading of the Megilla
RYbL: for they too were in that miracle
RYbL: when Purim falls on Shabbat, one asks and expounds the matter of the day
the baraita: Moshe enacted that Israel ask and expound the matter of the day -- Pesach laws on Pesach, Shavuot laws on Shavuot, Sukkot laws on Sukkot
taught by the dictum's mention of Purim: one does not decree against expounding on a Shabbat Purim on account of Rabba's concern (4b.21: lest one carry the Megilla)
RYbL: a person must read the Megilla at night and repeat it by day
RYbL's verse: 'my God, I call by day and You do not answer, and at night, and there is no silence for me' (Tehillim 22:3)
they understood: read it at night and study its mishna by day
R' Chiyya bar Abba's explanation: as people say 'I will finish this section and repeat it' -- 'repeat it' means read it again
Ulla Bira'a's verse: 'so that my glory may sing to You and not be silent' (Tehillim 30:13)
